title: The American Military Record — Source Discovery
coverageStatus: Incomplete discovery pass. Sources located do not imply that every engagement has been identified or every field verified.
scope: Federal and Continental forces; state and territorial militias; local armed defenders and privateers in associated conflicts; foreign, domestic, and U.S.–Indigenous actions. Context-only sources are not counted as engagements.
referencePolicy: Favor relevant primary, official, tribal, museum, university, and archival sources. Cap each engagement at 15 distinct useful references; do not fill the cap with duplicates.

candidates.note: Ninth Cavalry catalogue; identify the report and exact place. Catalogue-only lead.

candidates.title: San Francisco Mountains fight, May
candidates.note: Ninth Cavalry catalogue; identify actual day and scouts. Catalogue-only lead.

candidates.title: Arena Blanca contact, July 19
candidates.note: Held catalogue-only entry. Recover the commander’s report and distinguish it from Guilfoyle’s Alamo Canyon / White Sands pursuit.

candidates.title: Canada Alamosa contact, January 24
candidates.note: Held catalogue row: the chronological table lists a late-January contact; compare the original return and the Ninth Cavalry’s February Maney account before fixing the date or treating these as different actions.

candidates.title: Candelaria Mountains contact, February 5
candidates.note: Held catalogue row. The alphabetical list calls the locality New Mexico while the chronological list says Mexico; inspect the field report before promotion or geographic normalization.

candidates.title: Canyon Creek scout action, November 3
candidates.note: The alphabetical and chronological lists both name the action. A narrative, scout identities and exact canyon remain to be inspected before promotion.

candidates.title: Carr’s return-route contact near Fort Apache, August 31
candidates.note: Held catalogue row. May be an additional contact on the retreat from Cibecue or a differently dated phase of that operation; do not inflate the September 1 post attack without a report.

candidates.title: Fort Cummings / Mexican-line contact, April 29
candidates.note: Held catalogue row; compare with the Ninth Cavalry’s April Maney narrative, which lacks an exact locality. No independent fight narrative has been recovered in this pass.

candidates.title: June 6 shooting into a naval apothecary’s home and subsequent naval arrests
candidates.note: Glass’s June 8 report accuses Nicholas Dern/Dorn and Henry Imhof/Imhoff; Lull later questions whether the motive was attempted assassination or malice. Actual naval arrest response exists, but the private criminal attack’s engagement scope and names need independent review.

candidates.title: McEwer’s Ranch / Guerillo Canyon, August 19
candidates.note: Probable naming overlap with the listed Gavilan Canyon battle. Resolve McEwer/McEvers, Guerillo/Gavilan and the civilian advance before creating any additional record.

candidates.title: Pistol attack on Marine Lieutenant G.R. Benson near Sitka guardhouse
candidates.note: Glass’s January 20 report dates the shot January 17. No injury and no identified assailant or established motive. Held because an isolated criminal assault is not automatically a military engagement; do not attribute it to a Native community.

candidates.title: Rockwell arrest following an assault on a miner
candidates.note: James Taylor’s arrest and confinement appears in the reports; precise action date and field-force execution need a closer check before adding another policing record.

candidates.title: San Carlos contact, September 30
candidates.note: Held catalogue row under Indian scouts. The action type, participants and relationship to the departing Chiricahua group remain unresolved.

candidates.title: Shoshone Agency / Fort Washakie contact
candidates.note: Heitman alphabetical list gives April 29. Fort Washakie and Shoshone Agency are aliases, not two counted engagements. Original report and actual opposing party require inspection.

candidates.title: Sierra del Burro contact, May 3
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Mexico. Establish the scout command, report and direct U.S. service participation; do not infer the opposing Indigenous community from place alone.

candidates.title: Taylor’s San Mateo / Black Range contact, August
candidates.note: Regimental narrative identifies Taylor and detachments of B and H but gives only August. The catalogue places a nearby contact August 16; establish whether this is distinct from Valois’s Cuchillo Negro fight before adding another event.

candidates.title: Cloverdale canyon contact, June 1
candidates.note: Held catalogue row: Sixth Cavalry and scouts. A narrative is needed to identify the party and distinguish it from the April boundary fights.

candidates.title: Executed Army anti-outlaw operations in Cochise County
candidates.note: CMH printed pp75–76 gives requests and broad pursuit orders; identify actual detachments and contacts. Do not turn the O.K. Corral civilian gunfight into an Army battle.

candidates.title: Fort Stanton agency police action, July 23
candidates.note: Held catalogue row explicitly lists Indian police. Establish whether it was an armed agency operation and identify the people targeted; do not mislabel it a federal Army battle.

candidates.title: Meadows Ranch / East Verde attack
candidates.note: The Army staff-ride reading identifies the ranch attack in the July campaign. Verify the date and armed-defender participation before treating a reported family killing as a separate military engagement.

candidates.title: Medicine Lodge, Montana contact
candidates.note: Catalogue gives July 9. Identify unit, parties and precise locality; do not confuse it with Medicine Lodge, Kansas.

candidates.title: Mexican attack on Loco’s retreating group, April 29
candidates.note: Tupper’s report describes Mexican troops attacking the group the next day. Nearby U.S. forces do not by themselves establish American participation in that combat; hold outside the main inventory unless a direct U.S. component is documented.

candidates.title: Scout contact near Fort Apache, August 15
candidates.note: Held catalogue row under Indian scouts. Recover the field report and relationship to Big Dry Wash aftermath.

candidates.title: Stein’s Pass contact, April 23
candidates.note: Potentially McDonald’s advance-party phase of the listed Horseshoe Canyon action. Establish a genuinely separate locality and command episode before adding another battle.

candidates.title: Tullock’s Fork contact
candidates.note: Catalogue gives November 8. A different Second Cavalry pursuit in March 1880 also starts at Tullock’s Fork; do not conflate the years.

candidates.title: Beaver Creek / Sweetgrass Hills contact
candidates.note: Heitman chronology explicitly aliases these names and alphabetical list gives April 14. Original report required; separate from April 19 Wild Horse Lake unless evidence establishes otherwise.

candidates.title: Big Horn, Montana contact
candidates.note: Alphabetical list gives August 11. Identify the underlying event and distinguish from Little Bighorn 1876 and the 1883 presidential escort expedition.

candidates.title: Enterprise’s East African port visits
candidates.note: Visits to Johanna, Zanzibar and Madagascar are documented, but no executed armed landing or hostile contact was established in this reviewed itinerary. Keep as exclusion context, not invented engagements.

candidates.title: Cusack’s arrests of Cherokee Outlet intruders
candidates.note: Report forwarded August 26 confirms an executed arrest, but possible overlap with the August 7 Rock Falls removal is unresolved. Do not treat the report day as action day.

candidates.title: Individual Cincinnati armory, street and courthouse firing contacts
candidates.note: March 29 fighting and the follow-up militia protection are listed. Compare the state adjutant-general report and contemporary accounts before splitting further episodes.

candidates.title: Possible separate May boomer expulsion
candidates.note: The compilation forwards preliminary information on May 15 but does not establish a distinct executed expulsion in that entry. Keep as an identity lead, not a dated May raid.

candidates.title: White Canyon cavalry and cattlemen fight
candidates.note: July 1884 pursuit from Montezuma Creek may be the Perrine/Wormington contact already listed. Resolve names and localities from the cited Carlisle correspondence before either adding an alias with certainty or counting a second event.

candidates.title: Wright’s guarded party of twenty-four settler wagons
candidates.note: Compilation describes a guarded party in October; establish the arrest identity and actual field date before separating from grouped autumn expulsions.

candidates.title: Additional Stillwater blockade contacts
candidates.note: Orders and reports include an internally impossible July 23 entry in a January 1885 sequence. The principal confrontation is listed; do not invent a separate July operation from this apparent printing error.

candidates.title: Arrest of George Davis and General Pautrizelle at Colón
candidates.note: Secondary leads describe a naval arrest and later transfer/execution; the exact date and original report passage still require verification. Do not turn the lead into an established April 1 engagement.

candidates.title: Attack on Lillie’s Ranch, December 10
candidates.note: The narrative distinguishes this from Fountain’s December 9 camp attack. Armed-defender participation and the precise ranch location need confirmation before a separate engagement record.

candidates.title: Bavispe Mountains scout action, June 23
candidates.note: Held catalogue row, distinct in date from the listed May 1883 camp attack. No inspected independent narrative yet establishes the June 1885 episode.

candidates.title: Josanie / Ulzanna’s White Mountain reservation raid
candidates.note: Printed p. 54 describes killings and captures among Apache reservation families in late November. Identify local armed defenders and military response; Crook’s interpretation of the attackers’ motives is not established fact.

candidates.title: Juniata investigation at Johanna
candidates.note: Naval archives finding-aid lead concerns a September–December 1885 inquiry involving Dr.B.F.Wilson and the sultan. Actual armed execution is not established; do not confuse it with the 1851 Johanna bombardment.

candidates.title: Kiowa–cowboy gunfire at the Word and Bugbee ranch
candidates.note: A September 10 note identifies Dodd’s report and an exchange of shots without injuries. Establish action day, Army participation and parties from the full original report before listing a separate contact.

candidates.title: Lang’s Ranch contact, October 10
candidates.note: Held catalogue entry with contradictory Arizona/New Mexico locality labels. Recover the Fourth Cavalry Troop F report and distinguish it from the later 1896 Lang’s Ranch action.

candidates.title: Opunto / Oputo scout action, June 21
candidates.note: Held catalogue-only row in Sonora. Spellings and exact locality need verification against Crawford’s and Davis’s reports.

candidates.title: Reported soldiers’ assaults and extortion in Seattle Chinatown
candidates.note: CMH printed p102 cites November 9 contemporary reporting but says later discipline is unknown. Inspect that reporting and DeRussy’s correspondence before promoting individual allegations.

candidates.title: Return of the exiled Nez Perce to the Northwest
candidates.note: The park history places Joseph’s people at Colville in 1885. Recover the Army escort and release records before framing this as an executed military relocation operation.

candidates.title: Swaine’s intervention after Beaver Creek massacre
candidates.note: Federal history identifies the Fort Lewis commander’s actual intervention to avert further violence, but provides insufficient operational detail/date to create another record.

candidates.title: Tacoma Army detachment movements during the anti-Chinese crisis
candidates.note: The narrative includes proposed Tacoma detachments and an actual prisoner-custody episode. Verify which troops actually entered Tacoma, rather than treating plans as executed city operations.

candidates.title: Anti-Chinese expulsion contacts in additional western towns
candidates.note: Requests, civilian violence and military action must be distinguished. CMH explicitly says a New Mexico troop request was not executed.

candidates.title: Chato’s delegation detention and September transport
candidates.note: The park brochure dates his party’s Florida arrival September 18. Recover the arrest and transport records to identify the earlier custody operation; do not presume the delegation’s imprisonment was the same event as the reservation-family roundup.

candidates.title: East St. Louis militia firing during the Great Southwest railroad strike
candidates.note: Locate Illinois adjutant-general and contemporary reports for the April firing and protection operations.

candidates.title: Rush opium seizure aboard City of Rio de Janeiro
candidates.note: Coast Guard chronology lead reports a350-pound opium seizure near San Francisco in 1886. Exact date and primary cutter report not yet checked; no armed fight is assumed.

candidates.title: San Diego sealing schooner seizure
candidates.note: A separate FRUS1888 release order mentions the American schooner San Diego with 1886 British seizures; its actual capture date and cutter need verification. It is not added from the British compensation list alone.

candidates.title: Apache Kid and fellow scouts’ Alcatraz transfer
candidates.note: The museum narrative confirms the scouts’ military confinement but not the transport date in the inspected passage. Recover the court-martial disposition and movement orders, and distinguish later civil custody.

candidates.title: Colorow campaign couriers, reconnaissance contacts and dispatch chronology
candidates.note: Search-indexed primary report contains additional named contacts and August 24–27 dispatches. Direct PDF fetch timed out; compare action and report dates before splitting further encounters from Fox Creek or correcting its day.

candidates.title: Individual militia contacts during the Louisiana sugar strike
candidates.note: State intervention and the later massacre are listed. Identify plantation-level fights and distinguish militia from civilian vigilantes.

candidates.title: Rincon Mountains contact, June 11
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Tenth Cavalry E and L. It may be a specific component of the listed Apache Kid pursuit, but a narrative is needed before promoting it.

candidates.title: Alleged U.S. supply of arms to Mataafa’s supporters
candidates.note: German correspondence alleged American material support. A specific independently corroborated executed U.S. military supply operation remains to be established; do not equate German allegations with a U.S. battle.

candidates.title: Five Apache prisoners’ children transferred to Carlisle, June 22
candidates.note: The chronology names Ira Goso, Chappo Geronimo, Eli Hunlona, Calvin Zhonne and Bruce Patterson. Recover the custody/transport record and resolve the departure post before adding this as a distinct military removal operation.

candidates.title: Galena’s August–September Port-au-Prince protection station
candidates.note: Ship presence August 18–September 15 is documented. An actual landing, evacuation or coercive encounter in that interval has not yet been established; a routine station is not counted.

candidates.title: Leary’s September demands against threatened Samoan attacks
candidates.note: The September 6 letter protests threatened burning of Manono. Correspondence and readiness do not by themselves establish a separate completed landing or combat action; the later executed November interposition is listed.

candidates.title: Pompey’s Pillar contact
candidates.note: Catalogue gives June 16. Underlying Army or tribal-police action is unresolved; do not invent a battle narrative.

candidates.title: Scout contact near San Carlos Agency, July 28
candidates.note: Held catalogue row. Scout identities, cause and actual armed action remain unresolved; do not infer Apache Kid participation solely from the date.

candidates.title: Battle of Vailele and Apia hurricane — non-U.S. battle / disaster context
candidates.note: The December 1888 German–Samoan land battle and March 1889 hurricane are not U.S. naval engagements simply because U.S. ships were present. Preserve context without adding false American battles.

candidates.title: Mescal Springs attack on Troop I, October 8
candidates.note: The regimental narrative places an attack by armed Mexicans after its fall 1889 camp-of-instruction paragraph, but the year is not repeated in the attack sentence. Two soldiers were mortally wounded. Recover the post return and establish the year and attackers before promotion; the action may belong with ordinary domestic anti-outlaw operations.

candidates.title: Navassa labor uprising of September 14
candidates.note: Private Black American contract workers and white company managers fought; the Supreme Court account identifies137 Black workers and11 white managers as U.S. residents. This was not a U.S. Navy battle. Pair with the African American community-defense pamphlet and Harrison’s account of abusive labor conditions before considering a separate civilian conflict entry. The later Galena custody action is listed.

candidates.title: North-bank Missouri River contact
candidates.note: Catalogue gives June 2 near the Little Missouri mouth. Confirm participants and original action report before listing.

candidates.title: Williams’s Blue Mountain / Monticello investigation, December
candidates.note: The state history describes an executed Army investigation and a December 11 report, but no encounter with the hunters sought. Preserve as a potential investigative operation rather than assert a battle or coercive arrest.

candidates.title: Thetis protective cruise off Guatemala
candidates.note: The ship’s Central American protection station and July 27 San José visit are documented, but an executed landing or coercive encounter was not established from the reviewed DANFS passage.

candidates.title: Tongue River Agency contact
candidates.note: Chronological catalogue includes the agency among 1890 entries. Table OCR separates date and place columns, so no day is assigned without the scanned page.

candidates.title: Winn’s Tanner / Garden Canyon search, October 27–29
candidates.note: Printed p. 20 cites post returns for an executed patrol that found no Indigenous party. Preserved as a search-operation lead; the association with Massai is explicitly speculative.

candidates.title: Additional 1891 Bering Sea warnings and boardings
candidates.note: NARA identifies charts recording named vessel warnings/boardings. This batch includes individually verified cases and four named seizures; it does not invent a full census of more than70 warned vessels from the aggregate.

candidates.title: Al-Ki anticipated mutiny
candidates.note: The September 9 appeal to Cochrane and his conditional promise of Marine assistance reportedly prevented trouble. No executed mutiny suppression is established, so the statement is not added as a completed action.

candidates.title: Briceville and Oliver Springs stockade seizures and militia movements
candidates.note: Separate July, October and November contacts need unit and date review.

candidates.title: Charco Renondo / Redondo contact, December 29
candidates.note: Chronological table places this in 1891; alphabetical entry prints 1861, an apparent year error. Hold until an actual report confirms the date and armed action.

candidates.title: Marion warns the sloop Challenge
candidates.note: NARA’s chart finding aid dates the contact August 29; Rush’s August 31 log describes a prior Marion warning and tow for repairs. Held pending the original Marion action entry to distinguish coercive enforcement from assistance. Not called a capture.

candidates.title: Môle-Saint-Nicolas fleet pressure and lease negotiations
candidates.note: Naval presence during Gherardi’s attempted lease negotiations is a concrete research lead; precise executed coercive-force actions, as opposed to diplomacy or threatened measures, need primary reconstruction before listing.

candidates.title: Morewood and other armed coal-strike encounters
candidates.note: Identify company guards, sheriff posses and state militia participation before classifying individual episodes.

candidates.title: Rancho Rendado Zapata contact, December 30
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Third Cavalry C. Establish the ranch spelling and whether this was a fight, arrest or fruitless scout.

candidates.title: Robert and Minnie neutrality detention
candidates.note: The schooner transferred arms to Itata. The Navy pursuit is established, but any separate detention/capture needs a primary date and proof of military participation rather than a marshal-only civil action.

candidates.title: Strother’s escort of Cheyenne people from Pine Ridge to Fort Keogh
candidates.note: The regimental chapter confirms an executed escort and an 1891 commendation, but does not separately date the action. Hold until the order or original report establishes whether this belongs to 1891 or an earlier period.

candidates.title: Torpedo-boat feints and attacks on Yorktown’s boat
candidates.note: DANFS describes provocative approaches and an attack on Evans’s gig during the Chile crisis, but exact dates, weapons, casualties and boundaries between incidents need the ship’s 1891–1892 log. The verified January 1892 refugee operation is listed separately.

candidates.title: Wounded Knee supply-train fight, January 5
candidates.note: Mooney explicitly describes another supply-train encounter on January 5, citing Colby. Compare the original Colby account and Army reports with Loud’s December 30 train action before counting this as an independent identity.

candidates.title: Army intervention in Choctaw political crisis at Tuskahoma
candidates.note: Published Fort Reno research identifies Hayes’s Fifth Cavalry deployment lasting nearly a month in autumn 1892. Inspect the original execution report before listing.

candidates.title: Army pursuit across the Idaho–Montana line
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 159–160. CMH explicitly describes two companies sent after miners on July 19 and returning the next day without finding them; Montana’s governor refused permission after the fact. This executed pursuit is included in the 1892 intervention’s notes, pending original reports for possible separate subdivision.

candidates.title: Buffalo switchmen strike military operations and street contacts
candidates.note: Use New York adjutant-general reports to separate the broad Guard deployment from individual firing or bayonet incidents.

candidates.title: Coeur d’Alene prisoner escorts
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 160–161. The 1892 intervention includes actual escorts on August 23 and September 9. CMH dates the August 23 shipment of 135 prisoners under three 4th Infantry companies. Original route and custody reports can support separate component entries; an escort is not a battle.

candidates.title: El Alazan near Roma contact, December 24
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Third Cavalry I and scouts. Inspect reports and distinguish the contact from Mexican-only revolutionary raids.

candidates.title: Further Suggs initial confrontation and Army restoration detachments
candidates.note: June 17 shootout is listed. Date and identify the preceding attack on returning troopers and subsequent official military response before creating separate records.

candidates.title: Inman, Tracy City and Coal Creek component clashes
candidates.note: Identify individual state-force contacts and distinguish private guards.

candidates.title: Near Grande operations, February 6–15
candidates.note: Held chronological-table range for Third Cavalry C. A multi-day entry is not proof of a separate battle on every day.

candidates.title: Palito Blanco search / contact, February 18
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Third Cavalry D. Verify whether this is the Gonzales-house search and whether actual military custody or fighting occurred.

candidates.title: Rancho Grominito contact, January 24
candidates.note: Held catalogue row for Third Cavalry A and G. No independent narrative inspected; locality spelling may be corrupted.

candidates.title: Army deployment to Antlers during Choctaw conflict
candidates.note: Published Fort Reno research identifies Guthrie’s Thirteenth Infantry deployment in April 1893. Inspect its execution report; do not infer that Army troops fired in the preceding Choctaw clash.

candidates.title: Black Week landing-force readiness in Honolulu
candidates.note: Barker’s December 19 instructions prepared a neutral protective landing force; the reviewed account does not establish another executed landing. Do not turn plans or readiness into an engagement.

candidates.title: Earlier Camargo customs sentry-box firing
candidates.note: Correspondence refers to a previous incident complained of April 28. The later June case is documented, but the earlier shooters and event date remain insufficiently identified.

candidates.title: Juan Manuel Zarrate capture
candidates.note: The War Department notice confirms capture and delivery to Fort Ringgold but gives no actual date or arrest site in the inspected note. Establish the executing detachment and distinguish transport from capture.

candidates.title: Las Tajitos Ranch contact near Brownsville
candidates.note: Held catalogue identity lead. Possibly the same January action as Dickman’s Echeverria fight; do not create a second event until locality/date reconciliation.

candidates.title: Mangas de Agua / Las Muias Ranch encounter
candidates.note: The March 15 note confirms a recent encounter in which Magus de Aqua was killed. The later February 23 / Las Muias account and Lowe, Shely and Black Seminole scout participation need direct field-report verification before a precise battle record.

candidates.title: March captures and surrenders of Garza-associated leaders
candidates.note: The note identifies March 7 surrenders and March 8 arrests, but the executing military/civilian roles are insufficiently clear. Do not convert every reported arrest into an Army battle.

candidates.title: 1894 coal-strike military eviction operations in Indian Territory
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 139. The Chicago discussion briefly references Miles’s delayed response to orders for aid in coal-pit evictions. Actual locations, dates, forces and execution remain to verify from the referenced correspondence.

candidates.title: Additional Rio rebel fire on American merchant vessels
candidates.note: Individual merchant-ship incidents preceding Detroit’s January 29 escort need names, dates and actual U.S. naval responses. Do not generate multiple American naval battles from a general blockade narrative.

candidates.title: April 25 alerts at Walla Walla, Spokane and Fort Sherman
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 122. These readiness orders are not completed interventions. Actual subsequent Spokane, Umatilla and Puyallup actions are listed.

candidates.title: Butte and Billings marshal confrontations with Hogan’s marchers
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 119–120. The CMH passage says McDermott tried to stop the group, but does not establish individual fight dates or firing in sufficient detail. Compare original marshal reports and newspapers before adding a Billings gun battle. Do not turn marshals into Army troops.

candidates.title: Chicago July 4–5 Blue Island and stockyard clearances
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 140–141. The executed bayonet/rifle-butt actions are included in the Chicago Army operation. Original reports should establish distinct unit, site and time boundaries before splitting every yard encounter.

candidates.title: Earlier Trinidad assault on the marshal’s deputies
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 125–126. The source describes the deputies being assaulted and disarmed before the July 4 Army arrival. A precise action day and the participants’ weapons require the underlying report. This precursor is not the Army’s arrest-support operation.

candidates.title: Enid–Pond Creek bridge attacks and individual troop contacts
candidates.note: The broad military intervention is listed; find military reports and dated local accounts for each separate contact.

candidates.title: Fry and Kelly industrial-army train seizures
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 119. The chapter identifies executed private train seizures and eastward travel, but individual dates, armed contacts and military interceptions remain to isolate. Their quasi-military names are not evidence that every member carried weapons or fought troops.

candidates.title: Further Northern Pacific local escorts and tunnel patrols
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 126,163. July 7–8 Tacoma, Spokane and Davenport patrols are included in the route-wide operation. Original unit logs can support finer site-by-site entries; no firing is established merely from a patrol’s existence.

candidates.title: General Order23 and unexecuted firing instructions
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 146–147. The doctrinal order and instructions permitting firing describe authorized behavior, not proof that every detachment opened fire. Development context belongs with the separate milestones work.

candidates.title: July 7 Calumet and Riverdale whiskey-warehouse guard
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 145. Sargent and25 men actually guarded the warehouses. This is retained as a named component/alias of the Chicago operation; a separate record can be extracted after the precise locations and duration are checked. It was protection, not an established firefight.

candidates.title: Kearsarge’s uncompleted Bluefields mission
candidates.note: Kearsarge wrecked at Roncador while proceeding toward the crisis and did not complete the proposed landing. Shipwreck/rescue may belong in development/context rather than a combat inventory.

candidates.title: Kneebone killing and attacks preceding the Wardner occupation
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 164. CMH dates John Kneebone’s killing by masked men July 3 and describes later abduction and attempted powerhouse destruction. Identities and individual action dates need primary reconstruction; these private actions are not Army attacks.

candidates.title: Native Army scouts in the Forsyth interception
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 120–121. Some later narratives add Troop L, 8th Cavalry / Cheyenne scouts. The reviewed regimental and CMH passages establish the 22nd Infantry but not that additional participation. Original Fort Keogh returns should decide the scout claim.

candidates.title: Ochoa revolutionary party’s capture in Pecos County
candidates.note: TSHA identifies Texas Rangers and federal officials, but not necessarily U.S. soldiers, in the 1894 capture. Establish an executed armed military/ranger action and actual date before promotion; do not turn his trial or organizing into a battle.

candidates.title: Proposed blanket interception of industrial armies on reservations
candidates.note: CMH printed pp 123. JamesJ.Hill requested that commanders turn back trains crossing military posts or reservations. Schofield opposed the proposal and Lamont refused it; not an executed military action.

candidates.title: Brooklyn trolley-strike militia operations and firing contacts
candidates.note: A major state-force lead for later research. Inspect New York military reports and contemporary accounts; do not simply copy every police encounter into the Army index.

candidates.title: Eastern Shoshone standoff with the Jackson Hole posse
candidates.note: State narrative describes a separate bloodless armed standoff but supplies no individual day. Further local/tribal comparison is needed before promoting it alongside the Bannock June 30 action.

candidates.title: Further removal of Apache prisoners’ children to schools
candidates.note: The chronology identifies renewed child removals and close military surveillance at Fort Sill in 1895. Dates, executing authorities and individual movements remain unresolved; do not generate one new action for every year of detention.

candidates.title: Kucheng massacre investigation and naval escorts
candidates.note: Investigatory and protection leads require an actual armed landing/escort report before inclusion. A missionary attack by itself is not a U.S. military engagement.

candidates.title: Marine chronology’s March 1 Yorktown guard at Seoul
candidates.note: The primary Yorktown log places the consular guard at Chefoo in January–March, records Charleston’s Seoul guard returning March 26 and Detroit’s relief preparations March 24. The chronology’s date/location is a discrepancy requiring original-source follow-up, not a separate counted landing.

candidates.title: Emmet Mine armed contact during the Leadville violence
candidates.note: Locate a dated account of fighting at this mine, distinct from the September 25 militia escort.

candidates.title: Lattimer aftermath: Pennsylvania militia deployments and contacts
candidates.note: The massacre is listed. Inspect state reports for the separate troop response.

candidates.title: Leadville mine guards, troop escorts and final withdrawal
candidates.note: Divide the continuing operation only after dated state reports are inspected.

candidates.title: Aguadores follow-up fighting, July 2
candidates.note: The July 1 land demonstration is listed from Miley and La Garde. Catalogue ranges and later accounts extend through July 2; inspect Duffield’s full field report before splitting or extending the land action, and do not duplicate the offshore bombardment.

candidates.title: Baracoa and Sagua de Tánamo garrison capitulations, August
candidates.note: Miley pp. 206 onward describes his August 12 departure and visits to receive capitulations without a U.S. troop escort. Distinguish surrender negotiations from the actual arrival of American occupation garrisons before creating separate land-operation records.

candidates.title: Cuban pursuit fighting west of Siboney, June 23
candidates.note: Miley p. 74 reproduces Wheeler’s report that Aguirre’s Cuban force fought toward Sevilla before Wheeler arrived. U.S. observation of wounded is not proof of direct U.S. participation in that separate firefight; do not silently convert an independent Cuban action into an American battle.

candidates.title: Guánica July 25 naval landing and capture

July 20, 2023 is its posting date only. Retained as a sourced identification lead; an exact action date or July action month is not inferred.

candidates.title: Pedro 11 evacuation of injured children in East Africa
candidates.note: The 2023 award citation does not give a precise action date in the inspected passage. Establish whether firing was ongoing and identify the casualty-producing episode before listing it as a distinct engagement.

candidates.title: Space Command full operational capability declaration, December 15
candidates.note: Primary oversight excerpt fixes December 15, 2023. Kept as a follow-on phase for fuller comparison with original capability criteria; do not substitute this for August 2019 establishment or treat basing announcements as completed relocation.

candidates.title: Additional daily Red Sea interceptions and land strikes
candidates.note: The wider daily catalogue contains many more contacts. Each needs a dated primary statement and service/platform identity; generic coalition or U.S. forces labels must not automatically be turned into Navy actions. Merchant-only attacks, foreign-only interceptions and missiles observed falling without U.S. engagement are not imported wholesale.

candidates.title: Further American air, drone and joint contacts, 2024
candidates.note: Continue incident-level military releases, mission reports, foreign records, local reporting and civilian testimony. This selected pass is incomplete. Coalition missions, casualty totals and statistical sorties are not automatically distinct American engagements.

candidates.title: Further contacts in the AFRICOM 2024 strike register
candidates.note: The November 7, 2026 gap review revisited this annual register and incorporated additional supported action records where found. Continue underlying unit logs, unresolved rows, independent accounts, civilian-effects evidence and duplicate/date reconciliation. The register and its import are not a complete or independently verified encounter log.

candidates.title: Western Iraq raid sub-sites and revised target identifications
candidates.note: The August 29 whole raid is listed. The update changes the death count and identifies four leaders but does not establish four separately countable raids or the precise U.S. units at each site.

candidates.title: AFRICOM register pointer 35791 — article identity unresolved
candidates.note: One annual-table row displays a 35791 article URL while its hyperlink repeats 35789. The inspected 35789 body establishes the April 16 vessel airstrikes, but cannot identify a second article or contact. No second engagement or action date is inferred from this malformed pointer.

candidates.title: Air Force and Space Force transgender-policy implementation deadlines
candidates.note: The May 9 memorandum and different active/reserve deadlines are identified. Deadlines are not evidence every separation occurred then; preserve individual service status and subsequent litigation dates.

candidates.title: Domestic immigration-detention sites and Guard perimeter roles
candidates.note: Military temporary detentions at the border are listed. Verify actual service/contractor/civilian roles and community or Native-nation accounts at other domestic sites; announcements of future facilities do not establish executed military custody.

candidates.title: Earlier same-name Southern Spear robotic initiative
candidates.note: The January announcement describes a planned autonomous-systems counterdrug effort. Do not equate its announcement date with the September lethal-strike opening or November formal naming of the later campaign.

candidates.title: Further American air, drone and joint contacts, 2025
candidates.note: Continue incident-level military releases, mission reports, foreign records, local reporting and civilian testimony. This selected pass is incomplete. Coalition missions, casualty totals and statistical sorties are not automatically distinct American engagements.

candidates.title: Further contacts in the AFRICOM 2025 strike register
candidates.note: The November 7, 2026 gap review revisited this annual register and incorporated additional supported action records where found. Continue underlying unit logs, unresolved rows, independent accounts, civilian-effects evidence and duplicate/date reconciliation. The register and its import are not a complete or independently verified encounter log.

candidates.title: March 16 Houthi attack claim against Truman strike group
candidates.note: Houthi statements claimed a missile and drone attack, while contemporaneous U.S. officials described interceptions and no strike-group damage. Keep the day-specific tactical reconstruction as a lead until the primary Navy account and sequence are compared; do not adopt a claimed carrier hit.

candidates.title: Renewed transgender policy implementation and separation stages
candidates.note: The May 8 statement follows a Supreme Court stay and promises implementation guidance. Compare actual service memoranda, changing court orders and affected-member administrative records before asserting discharge outcomes or a single uniform completion date.

candidates.title: Absolute Resolve local contacts and casualty reconstruction
candidates.note: The overnight whole is listed with the official date-wording discrepancy. Named ground subtargets, civilian harm, the custody sequence and opposing-force claims need independent local and primary comparison before additional component entries are created.

candidates.title: Additional individual Iranian vessel losses and naval attacks
candidates.note: The fact sheet and briefing give aggregate losses and targets. Ship identity, exact date, American platform and hostile or accidental cause require separate verification; no independent sinking is manufactured from a total.

candidates.title: Additional tanker seizures: M Sophia, Veronica, Sagitta and Veronica III
candidates.note: The primary report establishes a wider executed tanker-interdiction series but does not provide a complete dated ship-by-ship catalogue. Retain these named discovery leads pending direct dated boarding statements; do not infer them from the aggregate total or conflate Veronica with Veronica III.

candidates.title: Further American air, drone and joint contacts, 2026
candidates.note: Continue incident-level military releases, mission reports, foreign records, local reporting and civilian testimony. This selected pass is incomplete. Coalition missions, casualty totals and statistical sorties are not automatically distinct American engagements.

candidates.title: Further Epic Fury air contacts and losses after the opening phase
candidates.note: Continue dated public mission and investigation records through October 31, 2026. Campaign assets and target lists cannot be paired to invent aircraft-specific strikes, and announced plans do not establish execution.

candidates.title: Further Guard street-shooting and custody incidents in Washington
candidates.note: The October 18 contact is identified from a current primary investigation notice. Other reported incidents require separate exact dates, force actors and original investigative records; no completeness claim is made through the research cutoff.

candidates.title: January 20 Golis Mountains register listing
candidates.note: The register supplies this date and general locality but no matching individual action statement was found in the bounded pass. Adjacent January 18 Lower Juba and January 21 Golis article publication dates must not be substituted. Hold for separate-contact corroboration.

candidates.title: January 26 Golis Mountains register listing
candidates.note: The register lists a northern Golis contact without distance or a matched individual statement. It differs from the southern January 25–26 Godane report, but a separate action is not promoted without identifying evidence. The repeated January 26 Godane row itself is a duplicate table row, not a new contact.

candidates.title: July 14 announced resumption of the Iran naval blockade
candidates.note: The inspected July 13 statement orders resumption for July 14 at 1600 Eastern Time. A later executed-operation report must establish the resumed phase before its announced start is promoted as completed activity.

candidates.title: June 3 JTF-North deactivation and personnel/assets handover
candidates.note: The June 4 release dates the colors-casing/deactivation ceremony June 3. This is separate from the listed January 15 JIATF-CC establishment. Future-tense personnel/assets transfer language does not prove every handover task finished at the ceremony.

candidates.title: Other Southern Spear strikes and survivor searches
candidates.note: Many additional dated strikes are shown in the wider primary and local catalogues. Public target-selection details and some service/platform identities are withheld. The selected entries here do not represent a full census; each remaining action needs an individual source pointer rather than division of aggregate numbers.

candidates.title: Possible additional April 7 Golis target or contact
candidates.note: The register has April 7 Golis rows at 63 and 75 km from Bossaso. Statement 36347 groups April 6–7 at 55–75 km and does not resolve separate April 7 contacts. One April 7 listing is included; an additional contact remains held rather than duplicating it.

candidates.title: Attack and burning of Fort Habersham
candidates.note: Haynes p. 281 reports the attack but calls it February while citing Roderick Easley to Jared Irwin, February 1, 1796 (Creek Indian Letters, Talks and Treaties, part 2, p. 463). The original letter and post identity/location must be checked before assigning a combat date or garrison. This is not silently dated February 1.

candidates.title: September attack on Colbert’s Fort and the Chickasaw towns
candidates.note: Piomingo’s September letter gives a detailed Indigenous account; Robertson’s October 24 letter (hp022) dates the attack to about September 20. U.S. ammunition support is identified, but an actual U.S. or American-volunteer combat unit is not established. Do not merge automatically with the May/Logtown volunteer action or treat the request for 100–200 men as their arrival.

candidates.title: British withdrawal from Fort Oswegatchie
candidates.note: The New York State Military Museum confirms British evacuation in 1796. Sources vary between June 1 and a later summer departure; no corresponding executed U.S. Army takeover has yet been identified. Treaty deadlines must not be substituted for a garrison arrival date.

candidates.title: Dutchman’s Point withdrawal and any American military reception
candidates.note: Discovery lead only: a lesser British post is listed among the treaty evacuations, but an American garrison, exact executed transfer and primary date remain unverified. No operation is promoted from a treaty-site list.

candidates.title: Eaton’s deployment to Colerain / Fort Pickering
candidates.note: Pickering’s November 26 instructions identify stores loaded aboard the brigantine for St. Marys and Colerain. Orders, loading and the intended mission do not by themselves establish the sailing, arrival or any armed intervention; those executed stages remain to be located.

candidates.title: Georgia frontier garrison and scout-duty returns
candidates.note: Fauche’s August 5 return documents militia/scouts and selected discharges at seven posts, including Fort Maurice service reaching back into 1795. Its column combines beginning-of-service and previous-muster dates. Hold routine station rows rather than invent seven battles or treat August 5 as the end of all frontier duty.

candidates.title: Rutledge party attacked on the Le Boeuf–Presque Isle road
candidates.note: The county history quotes Denny’s May 29 letter about four travelers attacked the previous Saturday, but also labels the incident May 22. The calendar wording and the travelers’ actual military/escort status require primary comparison before creating an engagement.

candidates.title: Separate September killing episodes at Harrison’s station
candidates.note: The proposed Carr’s Bluff record groups related killings. Primary depositions and Barnard’s correspondence are needed to separate the first five victims, subsequent Yuchi victims and differing aggregate counts; no invented day or additional independent massacre count is assigned now.

candidates.title: Retaliatory attacks near Carr’s Bluff and on the Altamaha
candidates.note: Haynes p. 280 describes subsequent household killings after the hunter murders. Original dates, places, defensive forces and any militia participation remain unresolved; these civilian attacks are not automatically called U.S. military engagements.

candidates.title: Burnt Fort on the Satilla versus Carney’s Cowpen
candidates.note: Jackson’s adjacent correspondence mentions both names, but equivalence is unproved. The site alias is withheld from the proposed Carney record; no second destruction is invented from the uncertain name.

candidates.title: Georgia custody of Indigenous hostages
candidates.note: The account includes May 20, 1795 payment for clothing and house rent for Indigenous prisoners under James Pearre. Payment dates do not fix each detention interval or identify the custodial military force. Held for custody/identity research rather than creating an arrest from an expense entry.

candidates.title: Exact day and primary Spanish evidence for the San Simón contact
candidates.note: Compare the thesis’s cited Spanish report or testimony for the gunboat action and its precise clock/date. The current proposal deliberately uses July precision and no casualty figures.

guides.title: Papers of the War Department, 1784–1800
guides.note: A discovery collection for frontier correspondence, federal and militia activity, military administration, and relations with Indigenous nations. Search individual documents before drawing conclusions about engagements.

guides.title: Continental and Confederation Congress records
guides.note: Finding aid for military, naval, state, territorial, and Indigenous-affairs records. Useful for tracking smaller actions and locating underlying records; this is not itself a battle list.

guides.title: Revolutionary War battlefield reports and survey resources
guides.publisher: National Park Service — American Battlefield Protection Program
guides.note: An entry point to battlefield surveys and preservation reports. Principal-site surveys help discover engagements but do not establish a complete list of fighting.

guides.title: Early History and Relationships Between Nations
guides.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian
guides.note: Cherokee historical context, homelands, alliances, and nation-to-nation relationships. Use alongside event evidence and histories produced by the participating Indigenous nations.

inventoryPass.policy: List identifiable individual actions before detailed research. Published lists are discovery provenance, not independent verification. Preserve unknown dates, captures without confirmed fighting, campaigns versus component actions, and unresolved aliases.

The principal assaults took place July 1, 1898; continuing trench fighting on July 2–3 is distinguished from the initial capture. The cavalry and infantry advances included African American regulars, other regular regiments and volunteers.

Evidence-based refinement of the original year-only date; existing content and research status are preserved. Chaffee’s expedition left the Tientsin area August 4, reached the legations August 14, and fought at the Imperial City August 15. The date refinement encompasses this land advance and its immediate culminating action.

CMH explicitly states that the General Staff came into being August 15, 1903. The February 14 legislation was an earlier enabling stage; refine the published year-only date.

Explicit proposed refinement of the published year-only date, for the attack and subsequent counterattacks/bombardment. French departmental account dates May 28–31; corroborating ABMC1938 paragraph 6198 describes the 72-hour bombardment from noon May 28. This is not merely the assault morning.

The raid and fighting at Columbus and Camp Furlong occurred March 9, 1916. Prieto’s detailed history and the Mexican museum narrative agree; occasional March 8 summaries do not replace this date. Villa’s forces attacked troops and civilians, and the Thirteenth Cavalry responded.
The linked official history and its landing chapter distinguish April 1–June 22 organized battle from preliminary operations, later mop-up and administrative campaign-credit ranges.
The official narrative explicitly identifies the September 13–October 15 battle interval and final capture on October 15.

The linked narrative dates the X-Ray assault November14 and the Albany ambush November17, with overnight withdrawal and relief November18. This dates the principal battles, not the whole Pleiku campaign or later casualty recovery.
